narrative:
On November 16, 2026, the Karnataka High Court achieved an overall hearing rate of 42.8%, successfully hearing 1,224 out of 2,859 scheduled cases across 53 roster lists. This reflects a noticeable increase in court efficiency compared to recent sessions, outperforming the 36.0% hearing rate recorded on November 12 (1,191 of 3,309 heard), as well as earlier benchmarks from September 3 (35.6%) and September 1 (41.2%).

Judicial performance displayed considerable variation across court halls. Notable high-volume clearances occurred in Hall 36 under Judge T.P. Vivekananda, who converted 82.0% of scheduled matters (50 of 61 heard), and Hall 23 under Judge V Srishananda, who disposed of 60 out of 83 scheduled cases (72.3%). Judge Geetha K.B. achieved an 89.7% conversion rate on a 29-case list in Hall 35. In contrast, several rosters registered no progress, including the division bench of the Chief Justice & K.S. Hemalekha (0 of 40) and the bench of Anu Sivaraman & K.S. Bharath Kumar (0 of 73).

Among procedural stages, Preliminary Hearings posted the highest conversion rate at 54.0% (198 of 367), followed by Orders at 45.4% (409 of 900) and Admission matters at 43.0% (373 of 867). Final Hearing conversion remained comparatively low at 29.1% (137 of 471), though it marked a significant rise from the 14.8% rate recorded on November 12. 

In terms of case types, Writ Petitions (WP) dominated the roster, with 609 of 1,315 cases heard (46.3%), up from 35.1% on November 12. Criminal matters performed strongly, as Criminal Revision Petitions (CRL.RP) reached a 63.8% clearance rate (60 of 94) and Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) reached 56.5% (78 of 138). Conversely, commercial and tax matters faced delays, with Income Tax Appeals (ITA) yielding zero hearings across 22 scheduled matters.
